status: machine-readable — only for the next AI session, not for human reading. Human-readable history/decisions live in PLAN.md and implementation-notes.md.
convention: This file carries POINTERS AND TRAPS, not retellings. A задача is cited by its section in PLAN.md or SPEC.md, never paraphrased here: a paraphrase is a second copy of the truth and it drifts (it already did once, for routing_lists). What belongs here instead: file and symbol pointers, measured facts, rejected shapes with their arguments, and the traps that cost the last passes time. Written down in full in implementation-notes.md, section 'doclint — утверждение документа о состоянии обязано опираться на исполнимое'.

citation_hygiene.rule: Every path, T/W number, policy name and git ref named in this file must exist. This is no longer a convention a human has to remember — `go run ./cmd/doclint .` checks it, and CI runs it as `go run ./cmd/doclint -git=false .`.
citation_hygiene.why_this_block_still_exists: It records what the check is FOR. Two consecutive passes cited 'Global Constraint 9, constraints.md' — a file that never existed in any branch — and the citation was what justified deferring a task that, when finally checked on its merits, cost one optional field and one wiring line. The rule that citation stood in for: a pass closes its own queue item and does not widen into neighbouring modules; where the correct shape does require changing another package, that is recorded in Deviations with an argument — it is not grounds to defer the task silently.
citation_hygiene.exceptions_list: docs/not-yet-written.md — the single list doclint reads. It goes red in BOTH directions: a line that has become unnecessary is a finding too, so the list cannot rot into a dumping ground. This round it went red in the second direction three times and was right each time: T25, T26, T27 and event_broadcast all had to leave it.
citation_hygiene.branch_names_are_not_citations: Cite commit SHAs, not branch names. Pass branches are deleted at acceptance, and doclint's git half then reds on a name that was correct when written.

closed_this_pass.shape: The queue offered two lawful answers — an end-to-end test or an argued refusal. The first was chosen, and the reason is the finding: the claim inherited by the queue ('сквозного пути через связку нет и в продукте') was half wrong. All five links existed (internal/agent/wire.go dialer wiring → internal/agent/dialer.go → engine.Dial → the intercepted system dialer in internal/engine/dialer.go → de.Report(a.hm), the single ReportFailure call-site). What was missing was a stand: internal/agent/harness_test.go builds the assembly on a fake engine, where two of the five links are physically absent. internal/agent/traffic_liveness_test.go builds it on a real Xray with only the device and the prober faked, both outside the measured path.
closed_this_pass.registry_correction: W31 lost its flag name: the row said `error_classify`, and measurement says the policy cannot redden it. A target-site failure reaches the client as end-of-stream, classify returns KindNone, and Report does nothing on KindNone — there is no verdict to switch off. The row now carries a dash and §6 names the reason. What actually holds W31 end-to-end is attribution by outbound tag (nodeFromContext in internal/engine/dialer.go).
closed_this_pass.controller_correction: None needed on the tests themselves; both negative controls were reproduced independently. A third control was added by the controller and is worth keeping in mind: removing the KindNone guard in DialError.Report ALSO leaves W31 green — the site failure is never attributed, so it never reaches Report at all. Attribution is the single mechanism W31 guards, and the §6 paragraph says so.

Not TCP — the argument §6.1 used against hiddify: a local port cannot answer 'who is on the other end', a unix socket and a named pipe with SDDL can, and writing that answer twice means two implementations to drift apart. acceptance_review.measured: Final main passes go test ./... , -race on internal/agent + internal/engine + internal/health + cmd/hop + internal/ipc, doclint, the full 47-policy negcheck with zero oracle defects, and the whole internal/l3 package under `HOP_L3=1 unshare -Urn`. go vet, gofmt -l and realtimelint were compared against a baseline captured on a6221d3 BEFORE the passes started: identical, line for line, no new findings.
acceptance_review.seam: The one defect of this round existed in NO branch alone and appeared only on the merged tree: the socket pass taught `hop status` to answer exit code 3 when no node is alive (§5.6) and to leave the service half of the JSON empty when the assembly answers; the L3 stand read the phase with exec.Command(...).Output() (any non-zero exit is an error) and only from the service half — while L3 kills its nodes deliberately, which is what all of T27 stands on. phaseAt in internal/l3/harness_test.go now distinguishes code 3 from a command failure and reads the phase from either half. Verified afterwards that the fix did not neuter the suite: T25 still reddens with the outbound binding removed.
acceptance_review.controller_rule_applied: Every incoming test whose subject is 'the mechanism exists' was reddened by hand by the controller, not accepted on the pass's word: W30 (wiring cut), W31 (attribution broken), W60 (fan-out in eventRing.push cut, one level deeper than the pass's own control), W64 (checkArgs disabled), T25 (sockopt.Interface removed), T27 (HOP_DISABLE=reject_mode). All six reddened.

parallel_passes_trap.what_worked: Three passes, zones divided per-file in advance, registry numbers handed out before the start (W60–W64 to the socket, W65–W66 to the traffic path, W67 to L3) and required to stand in the test NAME. No collision. Two of the three reserved ranges went unused — the traffic pass closed the existing W30/W31 rows and L3 needed no new number — so W65, W66 and W67 are free again.
parallel_passes_trap.what_the_zones_caught: Only ONE merge conflict per merge, and always the same place: the tail of implementation-notes.md. The §5.8 table and the §6 flag table merged themselves this time because the passes appended at different offsets. internal/policy/policies.go was touched by two passes and auto-merged cleanly — different regions of one file is not a conflict.
parallel_passes_trap.what_the_zones_CANNOT_catch: The seam in acceptance_review. Zones divide files; they cannot divide a CONTRACT that one pass changes and another consumes. The socket pass changed what `hop status --json` returns (both exit code and shape); the L3 pass consumed it. Each was correct alone, both gates were green, and the defect existed only after the merge. The rule that follows: after merging parallel passes, re-run any suite that drives the product through its real binaries — a per-branch gate structurally cannot see this class.
parallel_passes_trap.rule_for_the_next_parallel_run: Hand out registry numbers in advance and require them in test names; name the zones per-file; expect to resolve implementation-notes.md by hand; and name in advance which passes CONSUME an interface another pass may change, then re-run those on the merged tree, not only on the branch.

next_task.name: `hop nodes` через сокет §3.3: список узлов при работающем агенте
next_task.why_first: It is the last place where the CLI surface still lies about what the product can do. Today `hop nodes` opens the store directly, and the agent holds an exclusive flock for its whole life, so the command refuses with code 1 exactly when the user most wants it — while the tunnel is up. This is the last of the three consequences the previous HANDOFF listed under honest_gaps; the other two (both phases in status, code 3 outside probe) closed this round.
next_task.shape_question: Measured blocker, not a guess: the §3.1 frame is capped at 64 KB and is meant for control messages, while §6.5 promises 200 nodes. Decide between paging over the existing frame and a streamed answer (the events path already streams frame by frame — see internal/agent/clients.go), and answer it with a measurement of a real 200-node store rather than an estimate. The rendering must go through the single emit() point in cmd/hop/output.go; the store's own view types (store.NodeView, store.GroupView) already cross the CLI boundary today and are the obvious payload.
next_task.trap: `hop probe` also reads the store directly and will hit the same flock. Decide deliberately whether it follows nodes through the socket or stays a store reader — it is the one verb that today observes code 3 without an agent, and W56's guard rests on that.

gate.rule_learned: The L3 line is now part of the gate, not an optional extra. It was optional, and the cost was measured this round: a pass that changed only the CLI surface (ef9027d) left the whole internal/l3 package red, acceptance ran the other five commands, and nobody saw it until the next pass tried to use the stand. Any pass touching cmd/hop, internal/ipc or internal/agent must run it.

notes.doclint: Fast. Runs in CI as `go run ./cmd/doclint -git=false .` — a checkout has neither the pass branches nor the full history, so the git half is off there and on locally.
notes.negcheck: runs every guard twice (with/without its policy) via `go test -count=1`; 47 policies as of this pass, ~25-35 min wall clock on this machine — this is expected, not a hang; don't rely on go test's cache. It needs permission to listen on loopback: a network-restricted sandbox creates false oracle defects. It has no per-policy selection: for a per-task gate run the new policy's own guard under HOP_DISABLE=<name> by hand; the controller runs the full one at the end.
notes.realtimelint: does not accept ./... as an argument — pass literally `.`
notes.l3_how_to_run: Build once, run under an unprivileged user namespace: `go test -c -o /tmp/l3.test ./internal/l3` then `HOP_L3=1 unshare -Urn /tmp/l3.test` (add `-test.v -test.run '<pattern>'` to scope it). This works without root — unshare -Urn grants CAP_NET_ADMIN inside the fresh netns. Reusing the built binary across repeated unshare invocations is much faster than `go test` per run. Note what unshare does NOT isolate: $HOME. The store is per-test through HOP_STORE for exactly that reason.
notes.known_red_that_is_not_yours: go vet ./... is red at internal/engine/dialer.go (copylocks in xray-core's SocketConfig). `go run ./cmd/realtimelint .` is red with 3 hits in internal/dnstest/realserver_test.go. `gofmt -l ./internal` reports internal/l2/dns_test.go. All three predate these passes; the honest gate is 'no NEW findings', compared on the full output rather than the exit code. A baseline capture before starting is cheap and makes the comparison a diff instead of a judgement.
